content.title: About
content.content: Burdock (Arctium lappa) is a perennial herb whose root is commonly cooked and eaten. Cooked burdock has a tender texture, a mildly nutty flavor, and is a traditional ingredient in Asian and Eastern European cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The root contains inulin, a prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.
In traditional Chinese medicine burdock is used as a tonic for the liver and kidneys.
Its dense, meaty texture after cooking makes it a popular meat substitute in vegetarian dishes.
Only the root is edible; the leaves and stems can be bitter.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Inulin promotes the growth of healthy intestinal microbes, improving digestion and nutrient absorption.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Burdock is rich in polyphenols and quercetin, which help neutralize free radicals and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Blood‑sugar regulation
items.content: Inulin slows glucose absorption, contributing to more stable post‑meal blood sugar levels.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: B‑vitamins and minerals such as potassium and magnesium aid normal immune function.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory effects
items.content: Burdock extracts have demonstrated anti‑inflammatory activity, which may benefit chronic inflammatory conditions.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to burdock, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Burdock can potentiate the effects of diuretics and blood‑sugar‑lowering medications.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large servings may cause gas and bloating due to its high inulin content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked burdock is served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, or salads. After boiling, it can be sliced and lightly pan‑fried for a crispier texture. Peel the outer skin and cut the root into strips before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked burdock in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Raw roots store in a cool, dry place for up to 2 weeks or can be frozen in sliced portions.
